hot.title: Generative Representation Learning for Scalable Latent Tokenization
hot.summary: RePR trains image representations to capture how context improves a generative predictor’s predictions of image patches. It uses this signal to guide a tokenizer, then generates pixels from that representation. On ImageNet, 50,000 generations yield FID 2.18 for RePR-78M plus JiT-L versus 2.36 for pixel JiT-L at nearly matched training compute. This compares training FLOPs, not inference cost.

hot.title: T2-z: Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents for Robotic World Models
hot.summary: T2-Z adapts an action-conditioned world model to hidden environmental variation by optimizing a compact latent from observed interaction trajectories, without labels for hidden factors. The trained model stays frozen during test-time adaptation. Across four real-world tasks, average tracked-state prediction error fell from 19.30 to 10.85 pixels and action success rose from 26.47% to 70.80%; these are task averages, not guarantees.

hot.title: Stay CALM: Calibrated Online Aggregation for Multi-Horizon Forecasting Under Delayed, Overlapping Feedback
hot.summary: CALM adjusts an online forecasting aggregator’s learning rates for correlated feedback from overlapping future targets, without changing the underlying forecasting models. It scales each rate by an estimated loss variance and an overlap factor, using horizon as a default. Across 90 pre-registered runs, its test MSE was lower than Proceed’s in 88, but calibrated BOA won most often.

hot.title: Route After the Answer: Measuring Answer-Specific Failure Information
hot.summary: The paper tests whether a verifier distinguishes correct from incorrect sampled answers to the same task, rather than merely detecting difficult tasks. Across five benchmark and model settings, Jev’s within-task AUROC ranges from 0.837 to 0.904. On reused GSM8K draws, a trained verifier exceeds the in-sample task-only ceiling, 0.932 versus 0.914. Selection gains depend on candidate-pool contents.

hot.title: Librarian Agents: Training LLMs to Curate Long-Context Workspaces that Anticipate Future Queries
hot.summary: Librarian Agents prepares a reusable hierarchical workspace of synthetic files linked to source documents, then uses a separate agent to answer later questions. The builder is trained with reinforcement learning using downstream answer quality. On BrowseComp-Plus, it improves accuracy over baselines by an average of 33 percentage points across two fixed answering models; this result measures answer accuracy, not cost.

hot.title: DiscoveryRSI: Recursively Learning to Discover Valuable Hypotheses
hot.summary: DiscoveryRSI records evidence, revisions, decisions, and contributions across hypothesis development, then uses histories to train agent actions and revise research workflows. Its hypotheses pair an evidence-grounded claim with an investigation plan, interpretation criteria, and alternatives. Across four life-science domains, automated weighted quality rose from 4.86 to 5.39 after two rounds; this measures proposal quality, not truth or completed discovery.

hot.title: HereBot: An Artificial Curiosity Engine for One-Shot Language Learning in a Non-Transformer Cognitive Architecture
hot.summary: HereBot learns words through a teacher-led dialogue loop rather than generating language from a pretrained model. It identifies unknown words, asks for definitions, and updates representations using information from replies, with curiosity signals guiding questions. In Session 1, its vocabulary rose from 1 to 29 over 49 turns; this is an acquisition observation, not a benchmark or controlled comparison.

hot.title: Learning Self-Orchestration in Decentralized Agent Swarms
hot.summary: MPT trains decentralized agents to learn actions and turn-taking. Agents bid; the winning bid also allocates learning credit backward, and counterfactual rollouts train bidding. On Minecraft’s Iron Pickaxe task, MPT earns episode reward 41.5 ± 5.9 versus 25.4 ± 4.6 for Graph-of-Agents with the same action policies and 32 seeds. The method relies on external rewards and restorable states.

hot.title: A Language-Informed Loss for Visual Generation
hot.summary: LILIE trains an invertible transform to preserve information useful for predicting captions from corrupted image features, then uses distances in that learned space as a generator training loss. Unlike a lossy tokenizer, it retains image information and leaves generation in pixel space. On 256×256 GPIC images, Pixel+LILIE lowers gFD from 66.84 to 53.01 versus pixel-only training in the JiT-T2I-g evaluation setup.

hot.title: Has GPT-6-Astra Achieved Embodied Intelligence?
hot.summary: GPT-6-Astra evaluates embodied manipulation and navigation in simulation and on real robots. It prepares a frozen task package from permitted demonstrations and can review actions proposed by a controller. On RoboDojo, in-context learning achieves 27.62% success at the standard action-step budget and 81.90% with up to ten times the steps. These protocol-specific results do not establish reliable physical deployment.

hot.title: Scaling Online Exploration for Robot Agents
hot.summary: RAX lets robots learn tasks by exploring actions and turning successful decisions into reusable programs. A frozen language model observes outcomes, revises code for perception, planning, and control, without updating its parameters or training a policy. The paper reports a 37.4-percentage-point average margin over the strongest prior learned model across five selected simulation comparisons, not all benchmarks or robot agents.

hot.title: Persistent Planar Memory for Video World Models
hot.summary: PPMem generates camera-controlled video while retaining a persistent 3D scene memory. It predicts oriented plane primitives from each video chunk, merges them into a pool, and renders depth from that pool to condition later chunks. In a 56-scene indoor ablation, its joint plane-pool system reached 70.3% δ<1.25, versus 64.0% without persistent memory; this tests the combined design, not planes alone.

hot.title: Extremal Direction-Complete Sets in an Integer Quotient Lattice: The First Three Cardinalities and Equality Cases
hot.summary: The authors find the first three distinct feasible sizes in a quotient lattice, requiring each point to have a neighbor in every indexed direction. They are 2^n−1, 3·2^(n−1)−2, and, for n≥4, 7·2^(n−2)−4; equality shapes are classified up to translation. For n=4, 23 is impossible; at n=3, the third size is 12, but its equality sets are not fully classified.

hot.title: Are We Overthinking One-Step Generation?
hot.summary: Priming Models train a one-step image generator by first reconstructing clean images from corrupted inputs, then matching generated and real examples in frozen feature space. On ImageNet, Priming-L reaches FID 1.19 in one network pass using 238.95 EFLOPs, versus Drifting-L’s FID 1.61 using 1,476.39 EFLOPs. This is about 6.2 times less reported training compute for this comparison only.

hot.title: Can Visual Generation Expand What Unified Multimodal Models Know?
hot.summary: The authors test whether facts learned through image generation become available to text-only question answering, using controlled fictional entities across seven categories. They find direct transfer is incomplete: SenseNova-U1 reaches 88% visual accessibility but 0% text accuracy on number questions. Interleaved image–text alignment raises GLM-Omni’s average from 12.57% to 26.86%, but results concern tested models and fictional facts.

hot.title: Terminal-RSI: Recursive Self-Improving Terminal Agents via Recursive Self-Rewrite and Policy-Refine
hot.summary: Terminal-RSI trains terminal agents through alternating cycles of verified self-rewriting and policy refinement. It preserves successful demonstrations to update the actor, then uses execution feedback to refine the policy while carrying a learned value critic across phases. Across four Terminal-Bench suites, the equal-weight Mean@3 rises from 20.68% to 50.58%; on LHTB, strict completions rise from 0/46 to 5/46.

hot.title: Neural Networks Are Already Clean
hot.summary: Mechanistic interpretability of neural networks is examined through neuron- and circuit-level studies of image models and language models, including experiments that track neurons during training and test explanations through activation examples, interventions, and attribution graphs. hot.title: AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning
hot.summary: AutoSFT helps an agent improve supervised fine-tuning by changing training data through a structured research loop. A meta-agent selects recipes, while separate execution and analysis agents handle training and propose data changes; synthesis adds verified examples. On Qwen3-1.7B-Base, analysis reaches 67.10 on IFEval versus 60.60 within 30 rounds, in single searches per configuration.

hot.title: StopWatch: Goal Grounding for Object-goal Navigation
hot.summary: StopWatch separates perception and policy models for open-vocabulary object-goal navigation. A perception model predicts visible object categories and goal distance from RGB, while a separately trained policy uses those cues with observation history to choose actions. Scene annotations supervise grounding at every demonstration frame. On clean HM3D-OVON validation-unseen, StopWatch reaches 69.6% success versus 60.8% for LightNav-0 in simulation.

hot.title: Training Language Models to Fail Gracefully
hot.summary: GracefulRL trains models to favor success over safe fallback and fallback over error, while preserving a learning signal for success. It optimizes a combination of the log probability of success and the log probability of avoiding error, without labels or an inference-time verifier. On AIME, Qwen3-4B-Base reduced errors by 88.8% with a 3.1-point success decrease, in tested settings.

likes.title: Hybrid Reasoning Agents
likes.summary: HybridAgent lets a tool-using language-model agent reason in continuous hidden states and use text for tool calls and answers. HybridLink aligns hidden states with the model’s input-embedding space, while retained attention-cache entries carry context across turns. At 14B parameters, it scores 49.5 average on WebWalker versus ARPO’s 40.5, within evaluations of Qwen3-Base models on 11 benchmarks.

likes.title: VideoJev: System One Model for Video Understanding and Interaction
likes.summary: VideoJev scores candidate time intervals to locate events and candidate answers for video questions, reusing one video prefix across queries through cached or joint inference. It reports 65.3 mean temporal intersection-over-union, versus 58.6 for its 4B backbone, and a four-benchmark QA mean of 74.3, near 74.9 for Qwen3.5-4B Thinking; evaluations cover grounding and multiple-choice QA, not agent workflows.

likes.title: VLA-$Δ$: Learning Physical State Transition for Vision-Language-Action Models
likes.summary: VLA-Δ trains a vision-language-action model to represent changes in task progress, object motion, spatial relations, and contact, then uses that representation to generate actions. Its transition targets supervise training but are not decoded at deployment. It reports 98.40% on LIBERO and a 5.5-percentage-point advantage over π₀.₅ across five real-robot tasks, without leading every task.

likes.title: Vela: User Behavior as Supervision Sparks LLM Intelligence
likes.summary: Vela turns users’ timestamped behavior histories into supervision for predicting future actions and answering rubric-scored questions grounded in past evidence. It separates visible history from future outcomes to avoid leaking prediction targets. Fine-tuning Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on Vela-Instruct raises VelaBench from 51.5 to 63.0, but this shows gains after training on behavior-derived data, not that behavior supervision alone caused them.

likes.title: LLM-to-Flow Distillation: Teaching Natural Language Goals to Scientific Generators
likes.summary: LFD adapts a flow generator to natural-language scientific goals by having a frozen LLM propose attainable sub-goals and judge sampled candidates, then training on positive-versus-negative preferences. It repeats this process as the generator changes. In GSK3β ATP-pocket design, LFD reached a mean GNINA CNNaffinity of 6.77 ± 0.11 pK, above reward-guided baselines; this is computational docking evidence, not experimental validation.

likes.title: Towards Agentic Robots: Model, Data, Environment, and Harness
likes.summary: The authors survey agentic robots as systems that use goals, observations, capabilities, and execution feedback to choose actions, gather information, revise plans, or recover. They organize prior work into four domains and seventeen overlapping categories. An external RoboDojo evaluation reports 22.48% average success across 42 simulation tasks, versus 19.34% for trained DM0.5; this comparison does not isolate feedback’s effect.

likes.title: Interaction-as-a-Judge
likes.summary: The authors introduce interaction-based evaluation: a computer-use agent operates an app, and a judge assesses the resulting trace. Gemini 3 Flash reaches 69.1% accuracy on pairwise preferences, versus 65.6% with code alone. GPT 5.6 Sol reaches 81.6% on requirement verification, versus 77.0%. Interaction feedback also repairs more initially broken requirements within five iterations, while requirement discovery remains difficult.

likes.title: DuoDiscover: Scaling Autonomous Discovery Beyond the Evaluation Bottleneck
likes.summary: DuoDiscover searches for code regions to optimize while building a target-specific, inexpensive evaluator for ranking edits. Workers explore with these yardsticks, test their rankings against full evaluations, and use full evaluations to confirm gains. In a 20-hour, four-agent vLLM comparison, it achieved a 1.92× geometric-mean gain versus 1.07× for Claude Code, a result limited to this setup.

likes.title: Jeva: System One Models from First Principles
likes.summary: Jeva decides among candidate sets by separately encoding requests and options, then refining the request state against reusable option representations. Its decision head supports set-conditioned comparisons and an explicit null outcome; option computation can be reused across requests. On long-document sets with complete option reuse, hybrid caching reduced median latency from 2,102.0 ms to 75.1 ms, a 27.98× speedup.

likes.title: Cowork-Gym: Synthesizing Interactive Work Environments at Scale
likes.summary: Cowork-Gym generates environments for agents working with people through shared files and tools. It builds tasks, workspaces, user policies, and hybrid checks, then runs and revises environments; simulated users respond to progress and can change inputs. Qwen models improve in most comparisons; Ours-27B scores 0.8400 on PawBench under OpenClaw, but WildClawBench is a weakness and the pool is not representative.

likes.title: Scaling Discovery Requires Forgetting
likes.summary: The authors test whether resetting search history helps agents improve stalled optimization tasks. They periodically clear agent sessions and candidate-history state while retaining the best candidate, allowing four-agent teams to restart exploration. On AHC014, forgetting gains 9.2% on average over 30 more proposals per agent, versus 1.4% for continuing; experiments do not isolate which cleared state drives the gain.

likes.summary: The Agentic Scientist coordinates research agents through parallel sandboxed investigations, shared conclusions, rubric checks, retrospective comparisons, and evidence-grounded writing. In a two-worker RL fine-tuning ablation, shared knowledge improved search progress but did not significantly change final best scores. On a synthetic multi-needle retrieval task, query-conditioned Doc-to-LoRA reached 98.0% exact-match accuracy; this result does not establish general retrieval performance.

likes.title: More Methods, Better Agents? A Reality Check on Self-Distillation in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
likes.summary: The authors benchmark ten self-distillation methods against GRPO across four tasks and Qwen3.5 models at 2B, 4B, and 9B, using a shared evaluation protocol. Across twelve task-model settings, PCSD has the highest equal-weight mean, 54.26 versus GRPO’s 49.68, but leads no individual setting, winning six, trailing five, and tying one; results are limited to this benchmark.
